description: Probability + statistics decomposed. Concentration inequalities (Hoeffding, Chernoff), martingales, sufficient statistics, exponential families, EM algorithm, bootstrap, multiple testing correction, causal inference, modern Bayesian methods (variational inference).

sub_mechanisms.name: Markov_inequality
sub_mechanisms.definition: P(X ≥ a) ≤ E[X]/a for non-negative X.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Weakest concentration. Basis for stronger inequalities.

sub_mechanisms.name: Chebyshev_inequality
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. From Markov applied to (X-μ)². Universal bound.

sub_mechanisms.name: Hoeffding_inequality
sub_mechanisms.definition: For bounded RVs: P(|X̄ - μ| ≥ t) ≤ 2exp(-2nt²/Σ(b_i-a_i)²).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation modern ML theory. Concentration bound for averages. Used in generalization bounds.

sub_mechanisms.name: Chernoff_bound
sub_mechanisms.definition: Exponential bound: P(X ≥ t) ≤ inf_s>0 e^{-st} MGF(s).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Tighter than Markov + Chebyshev. Standard in algorithm analysis + ML.

sub_mechanisms.name: martingale
sub_mechanisms.definition: Process where E[X_{n+1}|X_1,...,X_n] = X_n. Fair game.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Gambler's ruin, stock prices (under martingale assumption), proofs.

sub_mechanisms.name: exponential_family
sub_mechanisms.definition: p(x|θ) = h(x) exp(η(θ)·T(x) - A(θ)). Includes normal, Poisson, exponential, gamma, binomial.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of statistics. Sufficient statistic T(x). Conjugate priors. MLE via gradient of A.

sub_mechanisms.name: sufficient_statistic
sub_mechanisms.definition: T(X) such that P(X|T) doesn't depend on θ. Compresses data.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Fisher-Neyman criterion. Rao-Blackwell improvement. Bayesian + frequentist.

sub_mechanisms.name: EM_algorithm
sub_mechanisms.definition: Expectation-Maximization. Iterative MLE for latent variable models.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. GMM, HMM, mixture models. Monotonic convergence to local max.

sub_mechanisms.name: bootstrap
sub_mechanisms.definition: Resample with replacement to estimate sampling distribution.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation modern statistics. Efron 1979. Empirical alternative to asymptotic theory.

sub_mechanisms.name: multiple_testing_correction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Family-wise error rate (Bonferroni) or false discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of modern statistics. p-hacking solution. Genomics + ML evaluation depend.

sub_mechanisms.name: causal_inference
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pearl's do-calculus. SCM. Distinguish observation from intervention.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. P(Y|do(X)) vs P(Y|X). Foundation of modern causal methods.

sub_mechanisms.name: variational_inference
sub_mechanisms.definition: Approximate intractable posterior by family of distributions. Minimise KL(q‖p).
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of modern Bayesian computation. Faster than MCMC. VAE foundation.

derivation_rules.name: concentration_inequalities_quantify_deviation
then: sample mean concentrates around true mean exponentially fast
derivation_rules.why: Hoeffding: exponential bound. Foundation of statistics + ML generalization. Universal.

derivation_rules.name: exponential_family_admits_sufficient_statistics
derivation_rules.why: T(x) = h(x)·1[x ∈ support]. Fisher-Neyman. Foundation of efficient statistics.

derivation_rules.name: EM_converges_monotonically
if: EM applied to latent variable model
then: likelihood monotonically increases to local max
derivation_rules.why: Foundation. Doesn't reach global max. Init matters. Standard for mixtures.

derivation_rules.name: bootstrap_estimates_sampling_distribution
if: data n samples, B bootstrap resamples
then: bootstrap distribution approximates true sampling distribution
derivation_rules.why: Empirical approach. Works for many statistics. Computational alternative to closed-form.

derivation_rules.name: do_calculus_distinguishes_causation_correlation
derivation_rules.why: Standard statistics gives P(Y|X). Causal: P(Y|do(X)). Different generally. Foundation of causal inference.
